stories.summary:
I think this is the Position Group that will dictate how successful this new Defense will be.... especially come Playoff time.



	 



	They have a real "Boom or Bust" potential, IMO, because each player has a question mark surrounding their season.



	 



	Groot:  Can he transition from McD's Defense and thrive in this new system?



	 



	Chubb: Does he have anything left in the tank, or go the way of Miller and Bosa?



	 



	Hoecht: Can he be as effective coming off a serious injury?



	 



	Parker:  How long will it take for the Rookie to adjust to the NFL game?



	 



	Solomon:  Will he finally be able to contribute in this attack-style Defense?



	 



	 



	My Prediction:



	 



	I really hope these guys can light it up this year....the Defense could be scary if they do, but I'm going to keep my numbers somewhat conservative.



	 



	Chubb: 8 sacks



	Groot: 7.5 Sacks



	Hoecht: 5.5 sacks



	Parker: 4 sacks



	Solomon: 1 sack



	 



	Total: 26......Over, but not by much.

stories.title: Yeah, Im a Homer, but National Media bias can be ridiculous..
stories.summary:
This article is from NYTimes/athletic giving their assessment on the Vegas over/under.



	Ive edited it to a comparison between the Ravens and the Bills reviews.



	He is not really concerned with Ravens new head coach, but thinks "Bills are going to regret replacing Sean McDermott with Brady".



	Also thinks Jackson as one of the top 5 QBs in the league is very important,  but never even MENTIONS that #17 guy for the Bills...



	Yes, the schedule is tough, but he finishes his comments by saying DJ Moore will be a bust, too, as the Bills have never been good at acquiring wide receivers....except he seemed to forget about that Diggs guy.



	Seems like too often folks create "facts" to support conclusions they have drawn rather than assess facts to draw a conclusion.



	 



	 



	AFC



	Ravens over 11.5 (+115)



	This seems like a big number with new coach Jesse Minter inheriting some old, squeaky parts. But Lamar Jackson is still a top-five quarterback, and last I checked, QBs are pretty important. He has a new coordinator, but that’s never affected Jackson before. The offense is going to score points (get Zay Flowers in fantasy) and Trey Hendrickson will give the defense a boost.



	 



	 



	Bills under 10.5 (+120)



	The Bills are going to regret replacing Sean McDermott with Joe Brady, and right out of the chute, too, with their first five games coming against the Texans, Lions, Chargers, Patriots and Rams. They also have a tough holiday stretch, with games on both Thanksgiving and Christmas sandwiched around road games against the Patriots and Packers and a home game against the Bears.



	I will be wrong if new receiver DJ Moore clicks (and if they ever find a decent off-ball linebacker), but there is nothing in Moore’s resume or the Bills’ history of acquiring receivers to suggest that will be the case.

Dion Dawkins loses 45 pounds
stories.summary:
Interesting that he was previously upset with fans for criticizing his weight, but glad he decided to do something about it. His weight certainly looked like a problem the last several years as he was getting beat in key moments, and even looking like he was taking plays off.
	 



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Dion Dawkins is going to have a new look ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins told USA TODAY's Ralphie Aversa at the 2026 ESPYs he was feeling "good" ahead of the upcoming season. The 32-year-old tackle acknowledged that was because of a key change he made for the campaign.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I've told [everyone] in the world that this will be the lightest season that I ever play," Dawkins said.
		

		
			Dawkins was listed as weighing 320 pounds by the Bills during the 2025 NFL season. The 6-5 tackle acknowledged he had dropped 45 pounds since his peak, though it wasn't clear whether his peak was his listed weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			What was Dawkins' goal in dropping that weight?
		

		
			"To play a little faster, play a little better because something is not getting us over that hump," Dawkins said. "So I want to be at the best that I could possibly be. So I said, (expletive) it, let's lose some weight."
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins noted he was still confident in his athleticism playing at a heavier weight. Still, he thought changing things up could benefit the Bills as they seek the right combination to get the team to the Super Bowl for the first time since 1994.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I am fast heavy," Dawkins explained, "but I might be just a little bit faster, lighter. And that might be what Josh [Allen] needs to get us over that hump."
		

		
			Of course, Dawkins also detailed that Allen hadn't yet seen him at the lighter weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"He'll probably see me and be like, 'All right, Dion, it's time to eat a little bit,'" Dawkins said. "But I would rather have that than all right Dion's time to lose a little bit. So I'd rather start super light and see how it goes."
		

		
			 
		

		
			The good news for the veteran tackle? First-year Bills coach Joe Brady is on board with his plan to drop weight.
		

		
			"If I come in lighter, I get a couple of the touchdown passes," Dawkins joked when asked about Brady. "So we'll see."
		
	



	
	https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/bills-o-lineman-lost-45-003413717.html
